analysis.one_liner: Solar Industries India makes industrial explosives and detonators for mining and infrastructure, and has rapidly scaled into defence ordnance, missile systems and ammunition for Indian and export customers.
analysis.whats_happening: In the June 2026 quarter (Q1 FY27), consolidated net profit rose 89% year-on-year to about Rs 666 crore on revenue of Rs 3,888 crore, with EBITDA margin expanding to 27.9%. Growth was led by defence (up 123% YoY) and international explosives (up 65% YoY), against an order book of Rs 21,350 crore. The stock hit a lifetime high after these results. Q2 FY27 results have not yet been announced as of October 18, 2026; based on last year's pattern (Q2 FY26 was reported on November 11, 2025), the next results are likely due in early-to-mid November 2026 - treat this as an estimate, not a confirmed date.
analysis.plain_terms: This is an explosives maker that has turned itself into a defence manufacturer - missiles, ammunition and ordnance now grow faster than its original mining-explosives business and carry better margins. The tension: profit is growing extremely fast (89% in the latest quarter), but the share price has grown even faster over the years, so the stock already prices in a lot of future success. If defence order execution or exports slow even slightly, a stock priced this richly has a long way to fall before it looks cheap again.
analysis.quarters: The trend has been one of accelerating growth: consolidated net profit went from roughly Rs 353 crore (Q1 FY26) to Rs 556 crore (Q4 FY26) to Rs 666 crore (Q1 FY27), each quarter ahead of the last. Segment-wise, defence is now the swing factor - up 123% YoY in Q1 FY27 - while international explosives (+65%) and domestic explosives (+52%) also grew solidly. Management has guided to about Rs 14,000 crore revenue for FY27, backed by the Rs 21,350 crore order book. No non-comparability or restatement issues were flagged in the results commentary found.
analysis.performance_read: Returns have been extraordinary and have far outpaced the Nifty: +42.7% over 1 year (Nifty -9.5%), +286.6% over 3 years (Nifty +16.8%), and +647% over 5 years (Nifty +25.3%). The stock did a 5-for-1 split in July 2016, which standard price series already adjust for, so these long-run returns are not distorted by that split. The current price is about 10.9% below its September 8, 2026 peak of Rs 22,455 - this reads as a normal pullback within a strong uptrend, not a crash, and should not be confused with one.
analysis.valuation_read: The stock is expensive by any conventional measure - trailing P/E estimates cluster around 90-97x and P/B around 28x (one older aggregator shows P/E ~65x and P/B ~17.4x, likely using a stale FY26 base; the higher TTM-based cluster is more current and is preferred here). Why it is expensive is clear: the market is paying up for a business compounding profit at 80-90% a year on the back of defence and export order execution. Whether that expensive price is justified depends entirely on whether this pace of growth continues once the current order book is worked through - that is a forecast, not a fact.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is both volume- and margin-led: revenue is up sharply (consolidated revenue roughly doubled YoY in Q1 FY27) while EBITDA margin also expanded by about 173 basis points to 27.9%, mainly because the mix is shifting toward higher-margin defence and export business. This combination - more volume plus a richer mix - is more durable than a pure margin story, but it depends on defence and export order flow continuing at this pace.
analysis.health_read: Reported debt is low (debt-to-equity around 0.2) and return ratios are strong (ROE roughly 30%, ROCE roughly 37%), suggesting financial risk is not the primary concern. Whether reported profit is converting cleanly into operating cash flow could not be verified from available sources - check the cash flow statement on Screener. The more relevant risk here is business risk: dependence on defence order timing, export clearances and government policy, not balance-sheet leverage.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters (the Nuwal family) hold roughly 73% of the company. Solar Industries has filed disclosures confirming promoters encumbered no shares during FY26 (year ended March 31, 2026); an older aggregator figure showing a small pledge (~2.3%) appears to be stale and is set aside in favour of the company's own exchange filing. No widely-tracked marquee public investor was found holding a notable stake in available sources - if you were expecting a well-known name on the register, it does not show up in what was checked.
strengths: Order book of Rs 21,350 crore gives multi-year revenue visibility
Defence segment revenue grew 123% YoY in Q1 FY27, now a major growth driver
EBITDA margin expanded ~173 bps YoY to 27.9% on richer product mix
watchpoints: Valuation is rich (P/E roughly 90-97x), leaving little room for a growth disappointment
Growth is concentrated in defence and export orders, which depend on government procurement cycles and can be lumpy
Dividend yield is negligible (0.05% TTM), so the entire return case rests on continued price appreciation
Stock is already 10.9% below its September 2026 peak, showing the price can move quickly in both directions
analysis.one_thing: The Q2 FY27 results (expected around early-to-mid November 2026) - specifically whether defence order execution and the 27-28% EBITDA margin hold up - will show whether the current premium valuation is being earned or merely hoped for.
analysis.data_notes: Cross-checked Q1 FY27 (June 2026 quarter) revenue, net profit, EBITDA margin and segment growth figures across multiple news sources, which were consistent. Valuation multiples (P/E, P/B) and one market-cap figure conflicted significantly across aggregators; the TTM-based cluster (P/E ~90-97x, P/B ~28x) was used and an older, lower FY26-based figure was set aside as stale. Promoter pledge status relied on the company's own FY26 encumbrance disclosure over an older aggregator pledge percentage. Exact FII/DII shareholding percentages and cash-flow conversion could not be independently verified - check Screener for current shareholding and cash flow detail.
